entities.name: AJH MiniMod (Eurorack module series)

entities.synthesis_method: analog subtractive voice built from discrete-transistor Model D circuit recreations

features.text: Individual modules plus ready-made multi-row systems and a keyboard version

constraints.text: Low internal signal levels make the modules sensitive to noisy switching power supplies

patching.summary: Patch cables on Eurorack jacks; some inputs are normalled through jack switches

facts.statement: The MiniMod range is a set of Eurorack modules that reproduce Model D (Minimoog) circuitry; the site says it works at standard Eurorack signal levels and system voltages and uses a Eurorack power connector and panel sizes.

AJH sells pre-configured MiniMod systems (e.g. a 6U starter with 3 VCOs, 2 sub-bass generators, mixers, 2 LFOs, 3 envelopes, 2 VCAs) and a MiniMod Keyz keyboard version pairing the modules with a Cre8audio Niftykeyz controller.

AJH recommends a linear Eurorack power supply and warns that some switching supplies inject ripple (stated up to 200 mV) that can disturb its low-level analog circuits; it also advises not mixing digital and analog modules on one bus board.
Oscillator built around a discrete transistor core claimed to emulate the earliest Model D oscillator card, with updated control-voltage summing for better temperature stability.
facts.locator: User Guide intro; VCO.html In Depth

facts.statement: Four simultaneous waveform outputs (shark-tooth, saw rising ramp, square, triangle), each about +/-5 V centred on 0 V with 1 kOhm output impedance.
1 V/Oct input accepts +/-7 V and tracks one octave per volt (may not track above about 10 kHz); Exp CV and Linear inputs accept +/-5 V; Exp CV level knob scales 0 to 120%.
Tune knob shifts pitch by about +/-8 notes; the Linear input adds up to about +/-7 notes; the Octave switch has a Lo setting that drops the oscillator into LFO range.
Square wave pulse width is adjustable from about 10% to 90% (50% at centre) by a manual knob and a +/-5 V PWM CV input with 0-100% depth.
Hard sync input expects a +/-5 V rising ramp (e.g. another MiniMod VCO's saw); a threshold knob sets sensitivity and a switch turns sync on (S2) or off.
The 1 V/Oct jack is normalled to the Eurorack power-bus 1 V/Oct line; plugging into the jack breaks the normal.
14 HP wide, 38 mm deep, drawing 55 mA from +12 V and 40 mA from -12 V; needs about 15 minutes warm-up before tuning.
Four-pole 24 dB/octave transistor ladder low-pass filter replicating the early Model D VCF, with a three-channel input mixer.
1 V/Oct input moves cutoff one octave per volt; the 1/3 CV input moves it 3 V per octave and the 2/3 input 1.5 V per octave, mimicking the original keyboard-control switches.
Freq CV level knob scales 0-130% of the Freq CV input; 1 V/Oct response occurs at about the 2 o'clock knob position.
Emphasis (resonance) is voltage controlled through a vactrol, can reach audio-rate modulation, and the filter self-oscillates as a sine VCO at high settings (about positions 8-10).
Three audio inputs accept up to +/-5 V; the signal path is AC coupled so DC CVs are not useful there.
An onboard jumper enables input overdrive; self-oscillation tracking is about 3-4 octaves and is not temperature corrected.
14 HP, 26 mm deep, 45 mA at +12 V and 30 mA at -12 V.
The product page says an output stage after the filter restores signals to about +/-5 V peak-to-peak modular levels (stated THD 0.008%).
facts.locator: VCF.html (product page, Core Voltages section) - fetched at https://ajhsynth.com/VCF.html

facts.statement: Two independent envelope generators recreating Model D contour generators; the response is Attack, Decay 1, Sustain, Decay 2 with both decays always at the same rate.
Each generator triggers from a gate input; any gate above about +2 V works and levels up to +10 V are acceptable; a manual trigger button is provided.
Attack and decay times range from about 10 ms to 10 s; sustain level is 0 to 8 V.
Output is typically 0-8 V but repeated fast retriggering can push it up to about 11 V; removing board jumpers J1/J2 lowers nominal output to 5.5 V with a peak limit of 8 V.
Retriggering accumulates level in a Model D specific way; a per-envelope decay switch selects decay active or instantaneous after gate off.
12 HP, 26 mm deep, 38 mA at +12 V and 15 mA at -12 V.
Glide circuit slews a pitch CV; processed input is 0 to +6 V (negatives ignored, above +6 V limited), output 0 to +6 V at about 500 Ohm; glide mode switch gives up/down, up-only or down-only.

Glide is active only while the Hold input is high (+2 to +10 V); when low the output holds the last value, so it also works as a sample-and-hold for 0 to +6 V; an unpatched Hold follows an onboard jumper (always on, or the power-bus gate).
Separate analog noise generator with white, pink and red (Brownian) outputs, each stated as +/-5 V peak-to-peak (wording of the manual).
Glide speed is asymmetric as on the original: upward glides are considerably faster than downward ones; the On/Off switch is not a bypass, equal to speed at zero.
6 HP, 54 mm deep, 35 mA at +12 V and 35 mA at -12 V.

Four-in-one module: discrete-transistor ring modulator with X, Y and Z inputs (Z being an extra resonant modulator input), a frequency-doubling switch, two shaped-sine sub-bass generators (-1 and -2 octaves), and a five-channel DC-coupled mixer.
Ring modulator, X, Y and the two subs are normalled to mixer channels 1-5; plugging into a mixer input defeats that channel's normal so the mixer can be used for audio or CV.
Mixer inputs nominally take +/-5 V (10 V pp) and up to +/-10 V can pass through; input 5 is much hotter and clips, with DC bias giving asymmetric clipping; subs are usable up to about 1 kHz.
facts.locator: Ring_SM.html top section; manual controls text

facts.statement: 14 HP, 24 mm deep, 55 mA at +12 V and 50 mA at -12 V.
Two discrete transistor VCA cores hard-wired in series: two audio inputs with level controls, two CV inputs and an offset for VCA 1, and a Master CV input plus level for VCA 2.
All CV inputs have linear response and the VCA is AC coupled (audio only); an onboard jumper selects a high-gain overdrive mode; the Master CV jack is normalled internally to +10 V when unpatched.
facts.locator: VCA.html Response, CV Inputs and High distortion sections

facts.statement: 10 HP, 26 mm deep, 40 mA at +12 V and 22 mA at -12 V.
MiniMod VCO and noise outputs are +/-5 V; filter and VCA cores run at lower original-voltage levels (filter core on +/-10 V from the +/-12 V rails) with output stages restoring modular levels.
facts.locator: VCF manual intro/controls; VCO controls list; VCF product page Core Voltages

facts.statement: Pitch CV is 1 V per octave; gates trigger above about +2 V and are accepted up to +10 V; internal envelope outputs normally span 0 to 8 V.
facts.locator: Dual Contour controls list items 1, 15; VCO item 3

facts.statement: AJH offers a blank MiniMod patch chart as a downloadable PDF alongside the module manuals; the page does not mention any electronic patch memory.
facts.locator: downloads.html file list (chart file name only; PDF not opened)

facts.statement: Two independent six-mode filters (A and B), each with mode select, input, output, cutoff, resonance, Q-Drive and gain, plus a crossfader and a MIX output; both filters self-oscillate at maximum Q.
Filter modes: LP2 (2-pole low-pass), LP1, BP1, HP1, HP2 and BR1 (notch).
Each filter has 1V/OCT, FM1 (attenuated, tracks 1V/oct at full), FM2 (attenuverter) and Q CV inputs; Filter A's 1V/OCT and FM2 inputs are normalled to Filter B's.
facts.locator: Manual p.6 FM1/FM2; p.10 jacks D-F

facts.statement: Series/parallel switch routes Filter A into B or runs both independently; DRY switches bypass each filter at the crossfader; phase invert on B; XFADE knob and XFADE CV with attenuverter set the MIX balance; Overdrive circuit is on Filter A only.
facts.locator: Manual p.8-9 controls 9-16; p.11 jacks G-H

facts.statement: With a typical 10 Vp-p Eurorack signal unity gain at the IN knob is about 12 o'clock; past that the input soft-clips.
20 HP, 38 mm max depth, 113 mA at +12 V and 102 mA at -12 V.
Described as the third generation of the Korgasmatron filter, designed with David G. Dixon; the manual refers to the classic MS-20 filter as the model behind the resonance behaviour Q-Drive counters.
facts.locator: Manual p.5 Overview; p.7 Q-Drive note

facts.statement: Intellijel's product page lists the module as out of stock at the time of access and describes it as an analog dual multimode self-oscillating VCF and crossfader.

The supplement shows the Korgasmatron II as a dual filter (A and B) with 1V/Oct A and B inputs (1V/Oct A is normalled to B), FM1/FM2 inputs, Q control and drive, and the modes LP2, LP1, BP1, HP1, HP2 and BR1.
facts.locator: Index; pages 01-08 (LP2/LP1, dual 1V/Oct sine oscillator, normalled inputs)

facts.statement: The supplement includes patches for a Korgasmatron II Expander adding AUX IN, AUX MOD and Q CV inputs for each filter.

Intellijel's legacy modules page lists Korgasmatron II, a Korgasmatron II Expander and Korgasmatron I (Corgasmatron) among discontinued products, and the manuals index links this illustrated supplement for Korgasmatron II.
facts.locator: Legacy Modules page text; Support page manual list (Korgasmatron II Legacy Illustrated Supplement)

facts.statement: The Morgasmatron manual calls Morgasmatron the third generation of the Korgasmatron design.

24-bit stereo multi-effects Eurorack module, 14 HP, with 32 effect algorithms (rooms, chambers, halls, plates, springs, church, gated, reverse, delay/echo, chorus, flanger, phaser, tremolo, pitch shifter, talk box, LFO filter, clipper, combinations).
facts.locator: Product page overview and features list

facts.statement: Eight-character display; PROGRAM/VALUE selects the program and adjusts values; buttons choose parameters 1/2 or 3 (up to three adjustable parameters per effect); a tap control serves time-based effects where the parameter table allows; FX SEND sets effect amount.
facts.locator: Product page 'Three parameters, one display' and 'Eurorack or line level'

facts.statement: INPUT LEVEL switch selects low level (Eurorack) or high (line) input; stereo input or mono into the left socket; stereo processed outputs.
14 HP, 100 mA from +12 V and 30 mA from -12 V; mounting screws and power cable included.
Church reverb decay runs 1 to 10 seconds; the LFO filter offers vowel settings A, E, I, O and U.
Behringer says the effects are powered by Klark Teknik; this is a brand claim not verified against a technical document.

Each of the 32 programs has up to three parameters: reverbs mostly Decay plus Pre-Delay/Damping (Bright or Dark); delay and echo Feedback 0-100% plus Tempo 72-500 bpm or tap; chorus Depth -20 to +20 and LFO speed 0.05-5 Hz; flanger and phaser Tempo 5-400 bpm or tap.
facts.locator: Quick Start Guide, 'SPACE FX Effects and Parameters' table (EN)

facts.statement: Two unbalanced 3.5 mm inputs (impedance above 22 kOhm), two unbalanced 3.5 mm outputs (330 Ohm output impedance); input gain switch is +2 dB (high) or -6 dB (low).

QSG states power consumption 90 mA (+12 V) / 25 mA (-12 V), 14 HP, 71 x 129 x 41 mm; this differs from the product page (100 mA / 30 mA), so the current draw is recorded as inconsistent between Behringer documents.
facts.locator: Quick Start Guide, specifications table; compare F-017-056

facts.statement: Controls are the display, a Parameter 1/2 button, a Parameter 3/Tap button, FX SEND knob, PROGRAM/VALUE encoder and an INPUT LEVEL switch; the guide lists no CV input, MIDI or preset-save function.
